You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From a83de90658280611933d6b3e5044726f63a953f2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yonghong Song <yhs@fb.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Feb 2019 22:18:16 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] selftests/bpf: set unlimited RLIMIT_MEMLOCK for
 test_sock_fields

This is to avoid permission denied error. A lot of systems
may have a much lower number, e.g., 64KB, for RLIMIT_MEMLOCK,
which may not be sufficient for the test to run successfully.

Fixes: e0b27b3f97b8 ("bpf: Add test_sock_fields for skb->sk and bpf_tcp_sock")
Signed-off-by: Yonghong Song <yhs@fb.com>
Acked-by: Song Liu <songliubraving@fb.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
---
 tools/testing/selftests/bpf/test_sock_fields.c | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/test_sock_fields.c b/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/test_sock_fields.c
index 9bb58369b481..bc8943938bf5 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/test_sock_fields.c
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/test_sock_fields.c
@@ -14,6 +14,7 @@
 #include <bpf/libbpf.h>
 
 #include "cgroup_helpers.h"
+#include "bpf_rlimit.h"
 
 enum bpf_array_idx {
 	SRV_IDX,
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the test `test_sock_fields` requiring more memory lock limits than the default system settings allow. Many systems have a low default value for `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK`, which can lead to a "permission denied" error when the test attempts to allocate memory beyond this limit. The patch addresses this by setting the memory lock limit to unlimited, ensuring the test can run successfully without hitting this restriction.

    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    Code statements:
    <text1>

    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the test `test_sock_fields` requiring more memory lock limits than the default system settings allow. Many systems have a low default value for `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK`, which can lead to a "permission denied" error when the test attempts to allocate memory beyond this limit. The patch addresses this by setting the memory lock limit to unlimited, ensuring the test can run successfully without hitting this restriction.
